findings.title: Account UI validation message switched to Java MessageFormat syntax
findings.body: The value was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The account UI uses i18next/react-i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` placeholders and does not understand Java `choice` format or single-brace `{0}` placeholders. As a result, users will see raw placeholders and the choice expression instead of a localized validation message.

findings.title: Admin UI validation message switched to Java MessageFormat syntax
findings.body: The value was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The admin UI uses i18next/react-i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}` placeholders and does not understand Java `choice` format or single-brace `{0}` placeholders. As a result, users will see raw placeholders and the choice expression instead of a localized validation message.

findings.title: Choice-pattern removal allows malicious HTML to bypass sanitizer
findings.body: In `normalizeValue`, for keys starting with `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit` or `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, the code replaces the entire `{n,choice,...}` block with `...` before sanitizing. Any HTML inserted inside that choice block is removed before the sanitizer runs, so malicious or unintended HTML in those translation strings will not be reported. These keys are used in email bodies and validation messages, which may be rendered as HTML, so this can allow XSS through translations.

findings.title: Lithuanian account message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The translation for `totpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This breaks the localized account UI for Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The translation for `loginTotpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. This breaks the localized login screen for Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Property files read with ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
findings.body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(fis)` loads the file using ISO-8859-1 by default, but Keycloak's message properties are UTF-8. This mis-decodes non-ASCII characters (e.g., Lithuanian, Chinese, Cyrillic), which can alter the values before HTML sanitization and produce false positives or false negatives. Use `PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))`.
